title: The Guy Who Traded A Paperclip For A House
sources: Wikipedia / BBC / ABC News - In July 2005, Kyle MacDonald began with a red paperclip on his blog One Red Paperclip and completed 14 trades over one year.
Town of Kipling, Saskatchewan - On July 12, 2006, MacDonald traded a paid movie role with Corbin Bernsen for a two-story farmhouse at 503 Main Street, Kipling.

lines.text: In two thousand five, an unemployed man started with one single red paperclip on his desk -
lines.caps: In 2005, | an unemployed man | started with | one single | red paperclip -

lines.text: and traded it all the way up to a two-story farmhouse.
Kyle MacDonald was tired of paying rent and had zero savings,
so he posted a classified ad offering to swap his red paperclip for anything bigger or better.
First, two women traded him a pen shaped like a fish.
The same day, he traded the fish pen for a hand-carved ceramic doorknob.
Then came a camp stove, an electric generator, and a snowmobile.
Each trade sounded completely ridiculous, but every single swap was real.
Trade number thirteen was an afternoon with rock legend Alice Cooper,
which he traded to a collector for a paid movie role.
Finally, the mayor of Kipling, Saskatchewan offered the ultimate deal:
the movie role in exchange for a deed to a renovated two-story farmhouse!
Fourteen trades, zero dollars spent, and he moved right into his new home.
